unchanged_claim.exact_statement: For every finite indexed family of nonempty physical supports, put t_j=2^(-width_j), rho=sum_j t_j and give each local subset law mass1-t_j to empty and t_j^2/(1-t_j) to each particular nonempty mask. Choose an actual anchor j with prior t_j/rho, force its local mask uniform nonempty and draw all other local masks independently in fixed order. The full physical-union output law is Q(A)=rho^(-1)sum_(z:union z=A)K(z)mu(z), normalized on nonempty physical sets; its optimal posterior is over the distinct actual pairs(anchor,local-mask-tuple), including allocation ambiguity. An exact two-array union/occupation dynamic program computes Q in O(2^n sum_j 2^width_j) rational operations. If the supports cover all relevant coordinates Q has full nonempty support. In particular for every finite nonempty list of positive clause widths w_j, U the product of disjoint OR clauses on those widths and F=2U(X)[1-U(-Y)]-1 on independent clones, the same anchor construction on both physical clause copies has complete nonempty actual-posterior cost C_Q(F)<155I(F)/24<7I(F). This is a new clause-mask reference, not an original-prime queue or a canonical partition-forest claim.
hypotheses: Uniform independent physical cube for the Boolean cost theorem; entropy and cost in bits.
Local support instances, the anchor draw and the canonical subsequent local mask draws are actual random choices; aliases or shuffled descriptions of one draw tuple are not counted as distinct runs.

The general pushforward normalizes for overlap, but its <7I payment requires the stated disjoint paired-clause Boolean family. No universal influence payment on arbitrary overlapping supports is asserted.
The new reference has its own explicit priors and local probabilities and is not claimed to be a mixture or subfamily of the original prime queues.
proof_source: SHARED_TAG.md sections1--5, including equation(2a) and the exact union/occupation recursion

unchanged_claim.exact_statement: For every r>=1 and widths w_j>=1, let U=product_j OR(X_j), with disjoint private blocks X_j of widths w_j, T=z OR U on one shared coordinate z, and f=2T-1. Put epsilon_j=2^(-w_j), a=product_j(1-epsilon_j), J=a sum_j w_j epsilon_j/(1-epsilon_j). Then physical I(f)=1-a+J. Let Q be the normalized A006 anchored clause-mask union law on supports {z} union X_j, with t_j=epsilon_j/2, empty mass 1-t_j and each nonempty mask mass t_j^2/(1-t_j). The fixed normalized reference R=(delta_{ {z}}+Q)/2 satisfies sum_{A nonempty} hat(f)(A)^2 log2(1/R(A)) <=(29/2) I(f); the standard empty/nonempty wrapper costs at most (33/2) I(f). For all w_j=2 and r>=4, the unaugmented Q instead has nonempty cross-entropy divided by I(f)>3(r-1)/224, although H(f)<6 I(f).
hypotheses: Uniform physical cube; all private X_j are mutually disjoint and disjoint from the one shared coordinate z.
Representation, z and widths are public before the spectral set is sampled; R is fixed for the whole spectral set.
Entropy and logarithmic code costs use base 2. Claims concern logarithmic cost with standard asymptotic arithmetic coding, not an uncharged integral prefix length.
